name: stock-omelette
title: File:Khao khai chiao packet.jpg
description: A packet of khao khai chiao (Thai script: ข้าวไข่เจียว): omelet with rice. This is often eaten for breakfast and is widely sold packaged at bus stations, train stations, or, as was the case here, in a shop belonging to a motorcycle service station for their customers to buy and eat whilst waiting for the repairs.

name: stock-balls
title: File:DFC 0302 A close-up of golden-fried meatballs and little red sausage pieces being scooped from oil with a wire skimmer.jpg
description: This photo shows a collection of deep-fried food items in what appears to be a cooking or straining process. There are golden-brown round balls (which look like dough balls or perhaps sweet dumplings) mixed with bright red pieces that might be fried chili peppers or some other red food item. The balls have a shiny, slightly oily appearance suggesting they've been freshly fried. They're sitting in what looks like a wire strainer or basket, likely to drain excess oil after frying. This could be a traditional snack or street food dish from various cuisines, possibly something like loukoumades (Greek honey balls), puff-puff (West African fried dough), or a similar fried dough preparation mixed with a spicy component.
